props.gloss_en: one who reads the Megillah may stand or sit
it was taught: which is not so with the Torah [one does not read it sitting]
whence this? R' Abbahu: the verse says 'and you, stand here with Me' (Deut 5:28)
R' Abbahu: were the verse not written it would be impossible to say it -- as it were, even the Holy One, Blessed be He, [stood]
R' Abbahu: whence that a teacher should not sit on a couch and teach his disciple [seated] on the ground? as it says 'and you, stand here with Me'
from the days of Moses until Rabban Gamliel, they learned Torah only standing
after Rabban Gamliel died, they learned Torah sitting
when Rabban Gamliel died, weakness descended to the world [hence the sitting]
the mishnah (Sotah 49a): when Rabban Gamliel died, the honour of the Torah ceased
and this is what we learned: the honour of the Torah that ceased is the learning standing
one verse says 'and I sat on the mount' (Deut 9:9)
and one verse says 'and I stood on the mount' (Deut 10:10)
Rav: [Moses] stood and learned, sat and reviewed
R' Chanina: neither standing nor sitting, but bowing
R' Yochanan: 'sitting' [yeshiva] is only a term of remaining
as it says: 'and you remained [vateshvu] in Kadesh many days' (Deut 1:46)
Rava: the easy [material] standing, the hard sitting
